name: Ellen Boone
life: “I still remember a class I rushed to in my warehouse shoes.” People around Harbour Bakery know Ellen by a small Saturday habit. Ellen buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I am taking an office course in secret. I want the conversion to include a room where I could actually learn.
appearance: Ellen has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for a dark undercut with a longer wave on top. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a black overshirt with pearl buttons with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. In conversation Ellen folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Ellen carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To find a training room inside the conversion.
family: Aubrey Yates is Ellen’s stepsibling. Ellen sets the time to leave. Aubrey picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The misplaced umbrella*, Aubrey says, “I manage the hotel that owns the stripes. I took the patched one to lunch and liked the shade better.”
connections: Lars James. A desk-job ambition gets its first practical offer from a warehouse evening student.

reactions.situation: A worker says their job was left out of the consultation
reactions.response: Ellen records the missing job in the worker's own words for the consultation.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Ellen asks the stranger who will be expecting them, then helps find a way to tell that person.

reactions.response: Ellen offers to accompany them while they tell the truth.
